The U.S. Army opened permanent anti-drone test lanes in Arizona, signaling a major expansion of counter-unmanned aircraft systems infrastructure and procurement [Army opened test lanes](https://news.google.?oc=5). This move highlights a strategic shift toward integrating autonomous systems in defense, supported by contracts for companies like Fortem and Echodyne. Concurrently, the Federal Aviation Administration certified the Garmin Autoland system for the Epic E1000 AX turboprop, allowing passengers to land the aircraft if the pilot becomes incapacitated [FAA certified Autoland](https://generalaviationnews.com/2026/10/01/faa-certifies-garmin-autoland-on-epic-e1000-ax/). These developments demonstrate a dual focus on enhancing defensive capabilities and advancing autonomous safety features in aviation.

In the autonomous vehicle sector, the Minneapolis City Council passed an ordinance requiring human drivers in driverless vehicles, reflecting growing regulatory scrutiny of local deployments [Minneapolis passed ordinance](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMi_?oc=5). This local action aligns with broader public concerns and legal challenges facing the industry, including a lawsuit settlement by Lyft and a challenge to the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration’s robotruck beacon waiver. Meanwhile, Amtrak introduced new Airo trainsets on the Cascades route, marking a step forward in regional rail modernization despite rising costs for high-speed rail projects [Amtrak introduced Airo trainsets](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwAFBVV95cUxNWVdtdkZreTJhSWpmV1VTODBnNTZqaVNDLVZQSThSa3ZPenlUN2dzYkpJWmtERVdsdXNOVDEwTmUtMWxpVXJHc25HQkRqcEI5dGZZeGhhWXhFOTlCWm42MDFLaWE0RFgtcERfTjhTR3JPdW1TUXJ4ZWpxMGVlZFFjOEdQR2otV0JGZWxQLUVvRnZTNGpvaDZkWF9BZVMtZ25RdGVEWjBPU2FvVXhORi0zSXUxaDBOaFUzUENPanZtMGE?oc=5).

The robotics sector is experiencing significant investment and expansion, with Agility Robotics appointing three new board members ahead of a public debut [Agility Robotics appointed board members](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijAFBVV95cUxNSjVLODFXZ1ZReHA0NU9RR0ptRDBqc0tvRmVXMU0wSE5YU25DMTgycjZlQ1ZYRFVtaGF0b0VuSy1fMi1keTJYUXZkWGM4VEM0ek8yazNvY0F1YUk2UUZ5VGI0dGNyOEFnNjdZempLcmltNFRsTE9uRzF6cEFSakFPSjBGdkNtbGdpZkVyZw?oc=5). Amazon is expanding its robotics manufacturing in Indiana, while Hitachi and Fanuc formed a strategic partnership for physical AI in manufacturing. Hyundai is preparing Boston Dynamics' Atlas robot for factory use, indicating a strong trend toward integrating advanced robotics into industrial applications. Additionally, NASA awarded $1.4 billion in logistics support service agreements to 16 companies to standardize operational costs [NASA awarded logistics agreements](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-awards-enterprise-logistics-support-services-agreements/). These actions demonstrate a commitment to efficient space operations and resource management.

International tensions continue to drive military technology developments. Ukraine showcased unmanned warfare at a NATO exercise, deploying 11 naval drones and 8 UAVs [Ukraine showcased drones at NATO](https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/other/11-naval-drones-8-uavs-ukraine-showcases-unmanned-warfare-at-nato-exercise/ar-AA2dp9t5?ocid=BingNewsVerp).
